nodes.description: Private constant bytes32 sentinel value used as the expected guard state.
Address state variable holding the external library targeted by the delegatecall in batchLogs; attacker-influenceable if set to a malicious contract.
bytes32 guard state variable initialized to GUARD_VALUE in the constructor and checked by batchLogs; the check require(guard != GUARD_VALUE) always fails as written.
Public mapping(address => UnlockSchedule[]) declared in the contract but never read or written.
Deploy-time function that stores the supplied library address into gatedLogBatcherLib and initializes guard to GUARD_VALUE.
Public, unpermissioned function that performs a low-level delegatecall to gatedLogBatcherLib with caller-controlled calldata, guarded only by a broken require check, then emits BatchLogs.
Constructor address parameter written into the gatedLogBatcherLib state variable.
Caller-supplied bytes payload that is ABI-encoded and forwarded into the delegatecall target.
Caller-supplied bytes32 value emitted in the BatchLogs event.
Boolean flag returned by the low-level delegatecall; its value is never checked.
Raw return data buffer produced by the low-level delegatecall; unused afterwards.
Unrestricted delegatecall to gatedLogBatcherLib executing abi.encodeWithSignature("multiSend(bytes)", logs) in the storage and value context of this contract.

edges.reason: Constructor parameter _gatedLogBatcherLib is assigned into the gatedLogBatcherLib state variable, fixing the later delegatecall target.
The constructor writes the constant GUARD_VALUE into the guard state variable, so the guard can never satisfy require(guard != GUARD_VALUE) afterwards.
Deployment-time execution determines the address later used as the delegatecall target.
guard is the access-control condition of batchLogs, but the inverted require(guard != GUARD_VALUE) makes the only possible state fail the check, leaving a broken/ineffective guard.
Execution of batchLogs unconditionally reaches the low-level delegatecall, the single dangerous sink of the function.
Caller-controlled logs bytes flow directly into the delegatecall calldata, allowing arbitrary external code to run in this contract's context.
The state variable gatedLogBatcherLib supplies the delegatecall target address.
The delegatecall produces the success flag, whose unchecked result means failed or malicious external execution is silently accepted.
The delegatecall returns raw data into the data local variable in this contract's storage context.
Delegatecalling arbitrary external code lets the callee re-enter batchLogs or manipulate this contract's storage mid-execution.
Caller-supplied contentHash is consumed by batchLogs when emitting the BatchLogs event.

normalization_plan.reason: The constructor parameter only serves to initialize state and is entirely subsumed by the constructor function node.
The logs parameter is a directly related input of the unsafe delegatecall operation and is meaningless without it.
contentHash is only used by the emitting function batchLogs for the BatchLogs event.
success is solely the receiver of the delegatecall return value and is subsumed by the unsafe operation.
data is solely the receiver of the delegatecall return payload and is subsumed by the unsafe operation.
